scope: Review of the actual-source-lanes verifier extension and preservation of pre-existing verification gates. This is a static code and recorded-evidence review, not an independent compilation, kernel replay, full proof acceptance, or mathematical completion certificate.

extension_gate_review.detail: The new group selects exactly ten fixed module names in a fixed order: eight reused/adapted supplier modules and two new consumers. The old groups, including the old twelve-module all group, retain their previous semantics.

The existing unchanged validate_project_closure function recomputes project imports from source, checks the exact target sequence, unique and valid module names, canonical module paths, source hashes, exact external imports and recorded module count. It requires full_external_kernel_replay_claimed to remain false. The reviewed closure snapshot has 72 project modules.

SOURCE_INTAKE.source_modules must equal the fixed target sequence. Each source path must be the canonical module-derived Lean path and each current source SHA256 must match the manifest. Extra, missing or reordered target entries are rejected.

The required recovered module is fixed to ImbalancedChen.Part3ActualCompletedSourceLanes. Exactly five ordered segment identities are required: completed_piece, signed_y_sources, zero_nonzero_source_split, positive_negative_source_split and completed_source_bridges. Each BEGIN and END marker must occur exactly once, and each extracted staged body is hash checked.

Where no mechanical repairs are declared, the staged segment hash must equal its recorded original hash. A nonempty mechanical_repairs record permits a declared source adjustment; the verifier does not purport to prove that such a description establishes mathematical equivalence. That remains a source-review obligation plus the strict/kernel checks. All five recovered segments in the reviewed metadata snapshot have no mechanical repairs.

Provider entries must have unique module names, be members of the independently validated closure, not overlap selected targets, and use canonical paths with exact SHA256 bindings. Both Part3ActualReciprocalSquarePoissonCore and Part3OriginalCommonPoissonKernelLanesCore are mandatory. Even if a closure module is not separately listed as a provider, the full validated closure is bound by source hashes and the preserved frozen-object pipeline.

All validated closure sources, both new manifests and the existing source/object regression test source enter the final source hash inventory. Closure source hashes are rechecked after intake validation; all bound sources are checked again by the unchanged final pipeline.

The new group explicitly describes actual finite-source common-J integration including reused suppliers, and excludes certification of OriginalData, sixSmoothMass and the whole P3.1 target. Reused suppliers and new consumers are recorded separately.

preserved_gate_review.evidence: Removing exactly two added constants, one group entry and the new selector branch restores the complete baseline AST. The actual saved unified diff is exactly the independently regenerated diff.

The old c509267 baseline ancestry/source checks remain in the byte-identical post-selector pipeline; verify_part3_distribution.py, Part3DistributionAudit.lean and verify_variable_envelope_boxes.py are byte-identical to c3999cc.
The original Lean token scanner is retained, and the baseline allowed axiom set remains Classical.choice, Quot.sound and propext. No axiom allowance or forbidden-token exception is added.

Audit rendering and baseline.validate_inventory are unchanged. The audit import/module list is selected for the ten concrete target modules, so supplier adaptation does not transplant an upstream owner count.
The exact Lean version/commit, resolved binaries, expected source head when supplied, clean worktree, package pins and package cleanliness requirements are unchanged.

After lake build of the selected target closure, selected objects are removed and each selected target is compiled with -t0 -j1 -DwarningAsError=true. Nonselected provider objects are frozen across this strict stage.
The bundled pinned leanchecker is invoked for each selected target, requires its expected replay success output, and is followed by the unchanged strict inventory audit.

The same object resolver and sidecar rules bind .olean, .olean.server and .olean.private in the local verified object tree. Path alias/symlink protections, provider freeze across strict compilation, all-object freeze across replay/audit and final object/source hash checks are retained.

Source-only execution remains explicitly SOURCE_ONLY_NOT_COMPILED. PASSED is reached only through the preserved formal pipeline. The extension does not convert an initial metadata snapshot or source-only gate into a proof certificate.

nonblocking_observations.detail: The inherited generic object-binding scope wording refers to a new consumer, while this new group's concrete selected set includes eight reused/adapted suppliers plus two consumers. The fixed target list, explicit new group scope and actual strict/replay loops govern the behavior. This is a documentation wording issue, not a weakened gate.

limitations_and_handoff: This reviewer did not run compiler, source-only gate, regression tests, leanchecker, cloud jobs or new remote source searches. The previously produced fifteen-test regression log was read and its hash matched the extension receipt; it was not rerun.

The final readback records the refreshed SOURCE_INTAKE and PROJECT_IMPORT_CLOSURE hashes. Earlier Task2 source-hash staleness was an announced intermediate snapshot and is not classified as a proof defect.

Root reports that all ten strict-probe targets and the refreshed source-only gate have passed. This review does not independently certify those runs; their exact receipts and the formal acceptance result remain the release evidence.
Provider objects are snapshotted after lake build under the unchanged verifier design. This does not claim fresh kernel replay of all seventy-two project modules or of external packages.
This result applies to the exact verifier SHA256 recorded above and the actual diff against c3999cc. A later code change requires a corresponding review.
